title: What is Mycelium
tagline: Agents as workers you compose, a room they share, and memory that outlives them: the ideas behind everything else here.
needs: Nothing yet. The exercise at the end installs Mycelium.
takeaway: The mental model the other courses build on, and a room of your own with a first task in it.
outcomes: Explain why agents here are workers, not assistants
Name what memory is for, and where each kind lives
Describe rooms, tasks and threads, and why chat stands apart
File your first task and hand it to an agent

quiz.question: What is a room's memory for?
options: Giving each agent a personality it keeps
Making the next worker faster and less often wrong
quiz.why: Memory holds preferences, behaviours and procedures, so a worker that arrives cold is useful at once. It isn't there to make an agent someone.

lessons.title: From one prompt to a swarm
A human drops a task, and never picks a protocol

quiz.question: Three agents are working three tasks. Where does their back-and-forth go?
options: The room's chat, so everyone sees it
quiz.why: A task is a row and a thread. Keeping the work in each thread keeps context focused, and the room's chat stays legible.

lessons.title: The aligner sits in the middle
Trust the workers, watch the outcome
What working like this asks of you
